prompt: High-quality anime footage. Near-future Gothic fantasy. Cinematic theatrical anime battle footage. High-density 3D Toon/Cel look only. Maintain theatrical-class key animation, high-quality compositing, smooth continuous motion with readable center of gravity, transparent lighting, and high-density background art. [Animation Direction] Explosive and sharp action. Sharp timing. Minimal anticipatory movements. Instant acceleration. Large, clear full-body movements. Strong contact recoil. Clearly leave inertia after contact. Dynamic camera integrated with movement. High kinetic energy. No waiting, long stances, long charging, slow recovery, or slow motion. [Role and Priority of References] <<<Image1>>> is the highest priority reference for face and character identity. Refer to facial features, age, eyes, iris, eyelashes, cheeks, jaw, bangs, horns, and drawings around the face. <<<Image2>>> is for costume, full-body design, and weapon reference. Refer to the same person's costume, decorations, body type, full-body silhouette, shoes, single long spear, and specific color scheme as in <<<Image1>>>. 3 is for tail reference. Refer to the connection position to the back of the waist, obsidian purple scales, a single tail naturally tapering from the base to the thin tip, and the purple light at the tip of the tail, same as the person in <<<Image1>>> and <<<Image2>>>. If there are differences between references, prioritize <<<Image1>>> for face, eyes, iris, jaw, age, bangs, and horns; <<<Image2>>> for costume, decorations, body type, and long spear; and <<<Image3>>> for tail connection position, scales, thickness, and tip shape. Do not copy backgrounds, text, frames, multiple panels, explanatory diagrams, or UI from reference images into the footage. [Fixed Protagonist] The protagonist is the same single dragon girl throughout. Maintain <<<Image1>>>'s small, delicate oval face, thin jaw, pale skin, small nose and mouth, large purple to amethyst eyes with multi-layered sparkle, delicate upper eyelashes, dark purple-black short bob with blue-purple highlights at the ends, and two curved black-purple horns on both sides in all cuts. Maintain <<<Image2>>>'s slender and well-proportioned body, black to deep purple high-collared Gothic costume, white chest cloth, thin gold edges and chain decorations, purple-black cape and wide sleeves, dark tights, black shoes, and single long spear. Maintain <<<Image3>>>'s single organic scaled tail connected continuously to the back of the waist, from obsidian purple scales to the thin glowing tip. Do not de-identify or simplify even in distant views or high-speed movements. In close-ups, return to the eye spacing, iris pattern, thin jaw, bangs, and horn positions of <<<Image1>>>. Maintain the same face, hair, horns, costume, body type, spear, tail, and color scheme; only facial expressions, gaze, breathing, combat stance, and natural delay of hair/cloth/tail may change. [Fixed Enemy] The enemy is a single, giant organic Yokai-Oni. Approximately twice the size of the protagonist, with soot-colored dark gray-purple rough skin, two ivory-colored horns extending backward, dark red glowing eyes, an ogre face with fangs, long messy black hair, a torn black-purple haori, and a single dark red glowing curse mark in the center of the front. Maintain the same design in all cuts; do not change into crystalline or crystal statues. Do not mix the face, eyes, hair, horns, costume, physique, or color scheme of the protagonist and the Oni. Avoid face averaging, costume swapping, cloning, or extra characters. [Shared Art Style] Line art is thin and delicate, line color is dark blue to blue-purple. Clear two-to-three-stage cel shading and pale intermediate shadows on face, hair, costume, horns, tail, and Oni. Shadows are centered on blue-purple and dark blue, not crushed to black. During movement, cel shadow boundaries should follow the 3D volume, with no flickering or irrelevant flipping. Color scheme is black, deep purple, amethyst, subtle gold, and soft white. Eyes and tail tip have multi-layered purple light, hair has thin blue-purple silk-like highlights, and skin is a clean matte anime style. Place incandescent areas only in narrow ranges at the center of contact, leaving high-saturation amethyst and black-purple around them to prevent whiteout. Distinguish cloth, metal, horns, scales, and glass with different reflections. Use directional motion blur only for high-speed parts; faces, eyes, hands, spearheads, and butts must be clearly readable. Soft cool white key light + weak warm fill on the protagonist's face. Background is low-saturation blue-gray and white-gray. Do not use thick black outlines, simplified TV anime style, flat coloring, generic 3D bishoujo faces, plastic CG, semi-realistic, realistic, live-action, or mixed art styles. [Temporal Continuity & Physics] Move stride, breathing, and tail sway from the start of the footage; no explanatory stills. The beginning of each cut inherits the end pose, speed, rotation direction, and screen progression direction of the previous cut; no re-posing, standing idle, or teleporting to starting positions. Supporting legs are fixed to the floor; do not slide soles at stepping, landing, or rotation pivots. Landing is sole contact -> knee compression -> waist sinking -> upper body follow-through. Spear reaction force is not absorbed by wrists alone; flow from elbow -> shoulder -> waist -> supporting leg to the next movement. Hair, sleeves, chains, capes, chest cloths, and tails are not integrated; they have different delays in the order of body -> hair/sleeves -> chains/cape -> tail tip. Hands maintain positions on the shaft; regripping is one hand at a time. Do not fuse fingers, wrists, and shaft; maintain front-back relationships of horns, hair, arms, spear, and tail. [Stage & Lighting] A near-future combat atrium with a giant glass ceiling and a two-level corridor. Thick white-gray structural beams, reinforced glass showing a pale blue sky, deep corridors, low-saturation mechanical equipment, and a polished light-gray reinforced glass floor. The floor softly reflects the girl, Oni, spear, and purple light. Clear parallax with three levels of depth: foreground beams, middle corridors, and distant glass walls. After falling, maintain the beam direction, light source, and vertical relationship of openings as the lower level of the same building. No readable characters, signs, advertisements, or logos. Uniform the direction of the cool white key light in all cuts. Blue-purple rim on the girl, Oni's dark red light reflects on the Oni and surrounding floor, and the girl's amethyst light reflects only on the girl, spear, tail, and nearby glass. No sudden exposure changes after large flashes. Do not hide faces, hands, spear structure, or Oni's curse mark with smoke or bloom. Use camera shake briefly only for strong contact and floor breakage. [Weapon & Tail] Only one long spear. Only the girl is the owner. Black long shaft, subtle gold decorations, one amethyst glowing spearhead, and one butt. Spearhead, shaft, and butt are always connected in a single straight line, maintaining the same total length, thickness, and decoration positions. No shrinking, bending, duplication, or deformation. Hands release only during throwing; order: empty hands -> same single spear in flight -> return -> grabbing the same shaft with both hands. During rotation, the entire spear revolves largely around the body as a single rigid body. Do not rotate only the spearhead; no transformation into propellers, windmills, or multiple blades. Only one tail. Continuously connected from the back of the waist; force is transmitted in the order of waist rotation -> base -> middle -> tail tip. No branching, duplication, or transformation into another creature. [Contact Causality] All contact must strictly follow the sequence: trajectory/gap/undamaged state before contact -> contact at specified position -> local light/crack/cloth displacement/gravity shift after contact. Do not generate magic waves, crystals, sparks, or glass cracks before contact. [Cut 1 | Approach] Rear diagonal mid-distant view near the floor. Start from the girl's back, camera moves forward as if catching up with the girl toward the Oni at the end of the corridor. The girl steps deep while keeping a single spear tilted diagonally backward and swaying a single tail low. Weight shift from heel -> sole -> toe. Cape and tail delay by half a beat. Shift axis over the Oni's shoulder, spear shaft crosses in front of the lens in foreground occlusion to a short close-up of the same face as <<<Image1>>>. Purple eyes catch the Oni, eyebrows slightly down, upper eyelids narrowed, mouth closed. Sink supporting leg and pass that momentum to the next rotation. Do not show the face static. [Cut 2 | Barrier Contact and Full Spear Rotation] Oni blocks the path with a dark red curse barrier. The girl doesn't stop, coordinates waist, shoulders, and hands to swing the single long spear largely around the body, continuous sweep from low diagonal to high diagonal. Hair, cape, and tail delay by half a beat. Camera moves diagonally around the outside of the shaft from waist-high mid-view, showing supporting leg, hands, full spear length, and contact point in the same motion. Thin gap between spear and barrier before contact. Short hit-stop only at the moment of contact. Thin amethyst circular wave is born only after contact, Oni's haori and messy hair flow backward. Connect reaction force to the next release. [Cut 3 | Throw, Return, Catch, Jump] Girl releases the shaft at the furthest point of rotation. Only the same single spear maintains a straight line, pulling a thin amethyst trajectory and flying toward the barrier. Oni tilts the barrier to parry, changing the spear's trajectory into a large return arc. Briefly show empty hands and the single spear in flight; girl grabs near the center of the returned shaft with both hands. Catch inertia transmits to upper body -> center of gravity. Kick the floor with that reaction force and jump over the Oni. Low close-up camera also rises along the spear's arc, changing from mid-view to full-body diagonal top view. Show throwing -> same spear return -> regrabbing -> rising in one sequence. Align spear with body centerline in mid-air, then turn to descent. [Cut 4 | Descent Contact, Crystal, Landing Rotation, Kick] Space between Oni's curse mark and spear tip before descent. Short hit-stop and narrow incandescent core only at the moment the spearhead contacts the curse mark. Only after contact, giant crystal ridges of obsidian purple -> high-saturation amethyst -> pale lavender rise in a fan shape. Crystals have three layers: thick main ridges, branching thin sub-ridges, and fine fragments. Translucent magic crystals of the protagonist's unique color, not bluish ice. Oni itself does not crystallize. Girl changes reaction force into a landing rotation, swinging the entire spear once diagonally. High mid-view camera also moves around the crystal in the foreground to the opposite side, flipping the axis from ceiling direction to floor direction. Briefly ground the same spearhead on the empty floor away from the Oni, rotate the body at a low center of gravity using the single spear as a pivot, and kick the Oni away. Small star-shaped cracks and purple light fragments on the floor only after contact. Oni's haori is displaced and full-body center of gravity retreats. Girl immediately pulls the spear and enters a dash. [Cut 5 | Upper Level Pursuit and Glass Breakage] Oni retreats to the upper glass walkway, turns to provoke with one hand, and blocks the retreat with dark red curse light. Girl kicks the floor without pause and dashes between beams, keeping the spear low. Eye-level mid-distant camera moves forward from behind the girl's shoulder toward the Oni's retreat path, showing the escape direction, the gap between the two, and the vertical relationship of floors. Briefly occlude with a beam and emerge on the direction-of-travel side. Glass floor is transparent and undamaged before breakage. After the Oni's step and the girl's spear butt apply pressure, it breaks from the action point in order: thin radial cracks -> polygonal planes -> large and small plate-like fragments that lost support. No liquid, ice, or snow-like pulverization. Floor breaks, Oni and girl fall to the lower level maintaining their vertical relationship. Thick rotating glass fragments reflect the girl's purple light and pale sky blue, connecting to the lower level with foreground occlusion where one fragment covers the screen. [Cut 6 | Lower Level Landing, Curse Bullets, Spear Defense, Barrier Breakthrough] Oni lands heavily on the lower level and fires dark red bullet-like curse rounds in a fan shape. Girl changes falling momentum into a landing rotation, continuously revolving the single long spear largely in front of her body with both hands. Spearhead, shaft, and butt move at the same angular velocity in a straight line, hands passing the shaft in turn. Camera rises from near-floor to waist-height, moving from outside as if passing under and over the spear, broadening from foot-level close-up to full-body mid-view. Purple and dark red light fragments only at the moment curse bullets contact the spear shaft or spearhead's path. Trajectories deflect to empty floor or beams only after contact. Do not let curse bullets adsorb or orbit the spear tip. Receive the final reaction force in the waist, change without stopping into a large diagonal sweep to push open the Oni's barrier, and pass that momentum to the tail strike. [Cut 7 | Tail-Only Contact] Contact-specific close-up. Oni's torso about 70% of the screen. No return to protagonist's face; spear is off-screen. From the left edge, a single tail same as <<<Image3>>> enters in a low horizontal arc, showing multiple scale segments leading to the body. Initially, a gap between the thin tail tip and the dark red curse mark. The tail is the only object contacting in this cut. Short hit-stop only at the moment the tail tip contacts the curse mark. Purple ring-shaped shockwave and thin light cracks only after contact. Haori -> curse mark -> messy hair react in order; Oni's full-body center of gravity moves backward, upper body pushed off-screen. Do not detach tail tip; maintain scale segments leading to the screen edge; the single tail returns naturally with elasticity. [Cut 8 | Collapse and Final Grounding] Receive the movement pushed out in Cut 7 with a low mid-view. Oni collapses quickly in order: one knee -> one hand -> upper body, remaining on the floor. Do not follow the falling process for long; only one bounce after grounding. Girl swings the single spear vertically down with the convergence of remaining momentum. Clearly leave undamaged floor surface between the fallen Oni and the spear tip before grounding. Amethyst spearhead contacts the empty floor in front, away from the Oni's outline. Purple and orange light fragments, small star-shaped cracks, and amethyst circular light waves only after contact. Do not collapse the entire floor. Final screen is a super low-angle close-up near the floor. In the foreground, the fallen Oni's hand and haori; in the center, a single vertical spear with spearhead, shaft, and butt connected in a straight line; in the back, the girl's bent knee and grounded black shoe. Leave a gap of empty floor between the fallen Oni and the spear tip. The specific moment the spearhead enters the floor is the final frame; cut immediately without holding maximum glow. No return to face close-up, chest-up composition, or static victory pose. [Audio] Synchronize low wind-cutting sound with the trajectory of the entire single spear. Hard spear sound + short magic resonance only at barrier contact. Leather creak + small high-pitched sound only at the moment of grabbing the returning shaft. Crystals: main ridge = low magic resonance, sub-ridge = glass-like cracking sound, fine fragments = high-pitched glass sound, synchronized to the order of generation. Upper glass: initial crack = sharp glass sound, plane detaching = low creak, fragments rubbing = thin high-pitched sound, falling = wind cutting. Curse bullets: short magic sound at firing, hard sound only at the moment of deflection by spear. Tail strike: air cutting + scale friction + dry cloth sound of haori + clear resonance of curse mark. Oni collapse: one floor impact + cloth sound of haori. End: synchronize hard spear sound, glass crack sound, and purple magic resonance only at the moment the spearhead enters the floor, cutting video and audio at that moment. No dialogue, conversation, narration, or singing. [Important Guards] Only one protagonist, one Yokai-Oni, one long spear, and one tail. No extra people/Oni, spear duplication, tail branching, or weapon transformation. The spear is a single continuous rigid body throughout. Do not duplicate even during throwing; grab the same shaft after return. During rotation, the entire spear moves; no high-speed self-rotation of the spearhead, helicopter-like rotation, propeller-ification, or windmill-ification. The tail is a single organic scaled tail connected to the back of the waist. Maintain connection position, multiple scale segments, and thin tip even during tail strike. Magic crystals are obsidian purple, amethyst, and lavender. Do not change into bluish icebergs; the Oni's body does not crystallize. The final spearhead grounds on the empty floor away from the Oni's outline, leaving a floor gap between the fallen Oni and the grounding point. No blood, dismemberment, exposed wounds, or cruel expressions. No text, subtitles, logos, watermarks, or UI.

prompt: Live-action running-shoe commercial. 20 seconds. No cuts are used. The background is one flat electric blue from beginning to end. No gradient, no texture, no floor, no shadows. The shoes fall continuously from the top of the frame towards the bottom. Dozens of running shoes are in frame at any one moment. They are all the same single model and differ only in colour: a light, thin running shoe with a thick white foam midsole under a brightly coloured knit mesh upper, with one small silver tab at the heel. That tab is the same silver on every colourway, and there is no gold or black metal anywhere on the shoe. The colours run through orange, lime, coral, dark grey, white and pale blue. Every shoe falls from top to bottom. They all fall the same way; what differs is that each tumbles on its own axis, so in any one frame some show their outsoles, some their sides, and some are seen from above. Any shoe that comes close to camera enters from the top of the frame and leaves through the bottom; none of them appears or disappears in the middle of the frame. The near ones are large and sharp; the far ones read only as small blurred patches of colour. Focus holds on one plane and everything in front of and behind it falls softly away. The camera holds its position, breathing very slightly. What carries the frame is the shoes. Partway through, a torn paper edge sweeps across the frame and opens the layer beneath it. Along every tear the white core of the paper is left ragged and fibrous, and a soft shadow falls onto the layer below. Wherever she appears, the camera is in front of her. It never follows her back or the back of her head; her face is turned towards camera. The photograph under the paper is black and white: high-key, with the sky blown out to white, and coarse darkroom-print grain. Even inside that black and white, the shoes keep their colour. One woman appears and she is the same person throughout: a Korean woman in her early twenties, with clearly defined features, long eyes and a narrow jawline. Her hair is deep auburn, falling in heavy waves to her waist, with a few fine braids running sideways from the crown. She ties it back in a single tail to run. She wears three things: a pale blue halter crop top underneath, a dark grey sheer cropped bolero over it with long sleeves and thumbholes that cover the backs of her hands, and dark grey joggers gathered at the ankle with a pale blue drawstring at the waist. She stays in all three while she runs; they never turn into a running vest or short athletic shorts. On her feet is the white-foam-midsole running shoe described above. (0:00–0:03) The film opens on the side of a coral running shoe filling the upper left of the frame, close enough that individual strands of the knit upper, the grain along the midsole and the stitching all read. It tumbles on its axis towards the lower right until the inside of the shoe comes into view. Behind it, dozens more come down at varying sizes. (0:03–0:05) A lime pair catches on the top edge of the frame with only the toes pushing in, close enough that the individual strands of knit mesh and the texture of the midsole are visible. The rest of the frame is blue, with only a few small shoes coming down far away in it. (0:05–0:07.5) LAND LIGHT fades up at the centre of the frame in white serif capitals with very wide letter spacing, fixed in place. Printed on paper, its strokes show horizontal printing lines inside them. One falling shoe drops in front of the letters and another behind them. From the lower right corner a torn paper edge rises at an angle and peels the blue layer away. (0:07.5–0:13) Where the edge has peeled back, a bright black-and-white photograph fills in. The camera sits low on the polyurethane track directly in front of her, facing her head-on and retreating as she runs towards it. The white foam midsole reaches forward, compresses as it meets the ground and springs back. The shoes alone hold their coral; everything else is black and white. The camera rises from her feet to her face and frames her from the front, chest up and large. Her eyes fixed straight ahead, her face wet with sweat and her dark auburn hair swinging all read clearly. The stands and the sky behind her fall softly out of focus, and the sky is blown out to white. (0:13–0:16) The torn edge rises from the bottom of the frame and the blue layer comes back. A coral pair falls through dead centre with one shoe crossing over the other, the camera further back now so the whole shoe reads. A single highlight travels across the small silver tab at the heel. (0:16–0:17.5) A single sheet of electric blue paper, come down from the top, covers the frame. Its lower edge is torn, with the white core of the paper showing. (0:17.5–0:20) A bright off-white paper field. At the centre, two lines of thin capitals: LAND LIGHT, RUN LONG. No other lettering and no symbol. A torn edge crosses the lower part of the frame at a very shallow angle. The final frame settles on exactly this. This has to read as a real commercial film. The print grain applies to the black-and-white layer only; the blue layers are sharp. Lettering appears in exactly two places: LAND LIGHT at 0:05–0:07.5 and the two lines on the final frame. No brand name and no logo symbol appear anywhere.

prompt:
Boy = a 15-year-old teenage boy, slim and quick, short dark hair, wearing a hooded jacket, jeans, and sneakers, a backpack on his shoulders. Alert, scared, determined, athletic. Appearance only.

Chasers = three older guys in their 20s, casual streetwear, moving fast and aggressively as a group in pursuit. Appearance only.

City = a gritty urban environment — narrow streets, alleyways, brick walls, parked cars, market stalls, and a quiet side street around a corner. Overcast daytime light, realistic city textures. Environment only.

SCENE: a tense cinematic foot chase. A teenage boy with a backpack sprints through the city streets, chased by three older guys. He races through a busy street, then cuts hard around a corner into a quieter side street and quickly hides out of sight — and when the three chasers round the same corner moments later, the street is empty and they've lost him. A clever escape, no violence — pure suspense.

TECHNICAL: 16:9, cinematic handheld chase camera, dynamic tracking and running shots, urgent energy, slightly desaturated gritty urban grade, motion blur, shallow depth of field, photorealistic thriller quality.

CUTS:
CUT 1 (0-5s): The boy sprints down a busy street toward camera, backpack bouncing, glancing back in fear. Behind him, the three chasers give chase, weaving through pedestrians and market stalls. Handheld tracking shot conveying speed and panic.
CUT 2 (5-10s): The boy cuts hard around a street corner into a quieter side street. Fast tracking shot following him as he ducks behind a parked car / into a doorway / behind a wall, pressing himself out of sight, breathing hard, trying to stay silent.
CUT 3 (10-15s): The three chasers round the same corner at speed — and stop. The side street ahead is empty. They look around, confused, scanning the deserted street, having completely lost him. Hold on their frustration as the boy stays hidden. He's escaped.

RULES: References are appearance only, do not recreate. Keep the boy's appearance consistent across every cut. This is a suspenseful chase only — no weapons, no fighting, no physical contact, no violence. The tension comes from the pursuit and the clever escape. Sound design: pounding footsteps, heavy breathing, urban ambience, a tense driving score that drops to near-silence when he hides, then holds on the quiet as the chasers lose him. Final frame on the confused chasers and the empty street.

prompt: [Style] Large-scale Japanese variety show water obstacle challenge special program (Japanese TV Game Show, Live-Action Broadcast), multi-camera real-time broadcast, 4K photorealistic photography, high-saturation summer colors, real-time throughout without slow motion. [Duration] 30 seconds [Reference] @ Image1 defines the challenger's face, hairstyle, body proportions, and full outfit. Use only the person. Do not use the grey studio background, the reference-sheet grid layout, or the multiple-view composition. Only one HANEUL exists in the video at all times. [Character] HANEUL — adult Korean female, early 20s, strong and healthy athletic build. Straight black chin-length bob with full blunt bangs, brown eyes, small stud earrings. Outfit exactly as @ Image1: fitted black short-sleeve crop tee, grey pinstripe pleated micro skirt with a plain white elastic waistband (no legible text), white ankle socks, black chunky platform derby shoes. She speaks only Korean. [Scene] Sunny outdoor large leisure pool obstacle course, five stages lined up from left to right. Stage 1: 5-meter high wooden jumping platform, Tarzan rope with pulley on overhead cable. Stage 2: 3-meter diameter red and yellow circular floating disc on the water, rotating continuously at a constant speed on an underwater axis, slippery surface. Stage 3: Four square floating blocks of varying distances, bobbing up and down with the waves. Stage 4: A slanted blue slippery climbing wall with grab ropes hanging from the top. Stage 5: A huge yellow cylindrical pipe spanning the water, wet reflective vinyl surface printed with red flame patterns, rotating continuously at a constant speed by a motor, just thick enough to be hugged by arms and legs, the right end connected to a small finish platform, directly below is a clear pool with no safety mats. Background includes palm trees, large water slides, light stands, commentary booth, temporary stands full of spectators. The entire film moves from left to right. [Screen Graphics] Top-left corner: a fictional program emblem — a hexagonal blue-and-red shield with a stylized white water-splash silhouette and the invented wordmark "SPLASH ATTACK". Fixed position and size, semi-transparent, present in every shot. Not based on any real brand or broadcaster. Top-right corner: a digital countdown timer in a rounded white box, large bold numerals with one decimal place. It reads 90.0 when the start buzzer sounds and counts down continuously and visibly in 0.1 steps (90.0 → 89.9 → 89.8 ...) for the entire run. It never counts up and never resets. It freezes at 63.0 the instant she falls into the water and stays frozen and dimmed for the final shot. Opening telop (visible 00:00-00:03 only, lower third): a pink-and-white broadcast nameplate — a magenta circle on the left containing the number "07"; to its right the name "HANEUL" in large bold letters with small katakana furigana "Haneul" printed above it; directly below, a red banner strip reading "Idol Trainee". The nameplate slides in from the left, holds, then slides out. No other on-screen text anywhere in the video. [Fixed Items] The position, size, color, and connection of the five stages remain unchanged throughout the film; only one challenger is always in the frame; hair and clothes are dry at the start and only naturally soaked after falling into the water; the circular floating disc and yellow pipe must be continuously rotating in all shots where they appear; the corner emblem and the countdown timer stay in the same corners at the same size in every shot. [00:00-00:03] Shot 1: Tarzan rope launch (Eye-level Medium → Wide Pull-back, ENG Camera) Visual: She stands on the edge of the 5-meter platform holding the rope, toes gripping the edge. Opening nameplate telop on screen. Timer reads 90.0 and starts running down on the buzzer, reaching 87.0. Dialogue (Korean): {I'll definitely clear this!} Action: When the buzzer sounds, she kicks off forcefully, the pulley slides right along the cable, her body swings over the water in a pendulum arc, black bob and bangs blown back by the wind. Commentary (Japanese): {First up, the Tarzan rope!} SFX: Start buzzer, pulley sliding, crowd cheering. [00:03-00:07] Shot 2: Landing on rotating disc (Fixed Side Shot) Visual: Fixed camera on the side of the floating disc, showing the person, rope, and disc. Timer runs from 87.0 down to 83.0. Scene: The red and yellow circular floating disc is rotating continuously at a constant speed on the water, the slippery surface reflecting light. Action: She releases the rope and lands on the disc; as soon as her platform soles touch, she is carried sideways and backwards by the rotation. She spreads her arms and takes small, rapid steps in the opposite direction to offset the rotation, knees bent and center of gravity low, stabilizing after a few wobbles. Expression: Eyebrows fly up, teeth clenched, then a quick grin. Commentary (Japanese): {It's the rotating disc! She held on!} SFX: Low-frequency hum of the turntable axis, sound of soles rubbing, a burst of cheers. [00:07-00:12] Shot 3: Floating board jumps (Dolly Track L→R) Camera: Dolly camera moving parallel to the direction of progress, tracking from left to right. Timer runs from 83.0 down to 78.0. Visual: Four square floating blocks bobbing up and down with the waves, unevenly spaced. Action: She jumps from the edge of the turntable, crossing the floating blocks with four consecutive single-foot jumps. On the second block she missteps, the block sinks sharply, her upper body lunges forward and arms circle wildly for balance. Her right foot splashes in the water before she manages to step onto the third block, and the final jump lands both feet on the fourth block. Dialogue (Korean): {Ah, it's dangerous...!} Commentary (Japanese): {She stumbled on the second one! But she recovered!} SFX: Muffled sound of blocks hitting water, splashing, intermittent gasps from the audience. [00:12-00:17] Shot 4: Slippery climbing wall (Front 3/4 Medium Shot) Visual: Front diagonal medium shot, showing the person, the sloped wall, and the grab ropes at the top. Timer runs from 78.0 down to 73.0. Scene: The blue slanted wall is covered in running water, reflecting light. Action: She runs up the wall, takes three steps, then her soles slip and she slides down a bit. She immediately drops her body to grab the wall, fingertips digging into the surface texture, and climbs again, right hand grabbing the rope hanging from the top, pulling herself up with arm strength. Expression: Neck muscles tensed, forehead creased, wet bangs stuck to her forehead, breathing heavily. Dialogue (Korean): {Heave-ho, heave-ho...!} Commentary (Japanese): {The slippery wall! She climbed it using only her arms!} SFX: Friction on the wet wall, rope tightening, applause from the crowd. [00:17-00:21] Shot 5: Hugging the rotating log (Rear Side Fixed Shot) Visual: Slightly rear fixed side shot, clearly showing the pipe is rotating. Timer runs from 73.0 down to 69.0. Scene: The yellow cylindrical pipe rotates continuously by a motor, a layer of water on the wet vinyl surface, red flame patterns rolling across the screen as it turns. Action: She jumps from the top of the slope and straddles the base of the pipe, clamping it with her chest, stomach, arms, and legs. The rotation immediately carries her to the right; she adjusts her center of gravity in the opposite direction and shuffles toward the finish by moving her arms and legs in small increments. Dialogue (Korean): {Uh, it's turning!?} Commentary (Japanese): {It's the rotating log! This is the most difficult part!} SFX: Low-frequency motor sound, wet vinyl friction. [00:21-00:26] Shot 6: Flipped over - Limit before finish (Front Close-up → Medium Pull-back) Camera: Front close-up at the finish side slowly pulling back to a medium shot, camera axis remains unchanged. Timer runs from 69.0 down to 64.0. Action: The pipe continues to rotate, slowly flipping her body to the right. Her center of gravity passes the highest point of the pipe and she can't pull it back. Her right leg detaches first, flailing

prompt:

Character: Protagonist @ Image 1
——————
[Shot 1 00:00-00:02 | Realistic Home · Spinning Record]
Medium shot, fixed camera, no camera movement. Indoor corridor, background is a creamy-white wall and a dark brown wooden door (hinges clearly visible), dim indoor warm lighting, the picture has realistic mobile phone shooting noise and slight exposure fluctuations.
The protagonist wears a white top with black floral print, thin-framed glasses, in a natural home state, standing on the right half of the frame facing the camera, expression calm and restrained, eyes looking straight at the camera, body almost motionless.
00:00-00:00.6 She lifts her left hand towards the left side of her body, her left index finger through the center hole of a black record, holding the record to the **middle-left of the frame** (not in the center, but obviously to the left), the record surface completely faces the camera, like a disc suspended on the left side of the frame.
00:00.6-00:02 She extends her right hand, fingertips touch the edge of the record, her wrist flicks hard—the record immediately spins at high speed around her left index finger. The record stays at that position on the left, spinning at high speed, size and position unchanged.
00:02 Hard cut (position matching). At the frame where the record spins fastest, the screen cuts directly—the next frame is a completely different scene, and at the position of the spinning record on the left, it perfectly connects to the rotating vinyl record control in the player UI, with position, size, and rotation direction perfectly aligned. Visually, it looks like the same record is spinning, but the world around it has changed.
——————

Close-up character shot. This section is not a live video, but a refined static poster given 2.5D parallax dynamics—no physical camera movement, only a very slow pseudo-push-in feel: slight relative displacement between the character layer and background layer, with foreground falling leaves moving fastest, the character following, and the background slowest, creating stereoscopic depth. - Top left: Golden serif large text 'FASHION', small text 'SELF-PORTRAIT' below, next line year '1901'.
- **Middle-left of the frame (matching the record position from the previous shot)**: A 3D vinyl record-shaped player control, rotating slowly clockwise, with her own circular avatar embedded in the center.
- Bottom left: Minimalist music player progress bar, with play/pause, previous, and next buttons, the bar slowly advancing over time.
- Left side also has light yellow and light gray magazine-style color blocks as layout decoration.
- No lyrics or sentimental text appears on the screen.
[Overall Tone] Shot 1 is realistic dim indoor warm tone; Shot 2 is rich autumn warm golden tone, strong sunlight, translucent skin, commercial poster quality.
[Sound Effects] Shot 1 is realistic indoor ambient sound + slight plastic friction and wind from the spinning record; sounds cut at the moment of the hard cut; Shot 2 cuts directly into full sentimental music (warm texture with vinyl noise), background is very light wind and leaf friction.

The overall image is flat, retaining realistic lens flare and slight edge chromatic aberration. Filmed from a student's perspective with occasionally imperfect composition. The girl uses Preset Character #1 in Preset Clothing #2. The boy meticulously cleans the girl's desk with wet wipes and places breakfast there while classmates tease him. 4-8s: Quick cuts of daily moments of him serving her quietly despite teasing. 8-11s: During class, the teacher asks about the girl's absence. The camera turns to the boy whose eyes redden as he prepares to speak. 12-18s: Continuation of the previous shot. The camera shakes from the sudden movement. 23-30s: The class bursts into laughter. The girl keeps pinching his ear while he looks aggrieved. The voiceover concludes mockingly. Section 1 | 0–10s

[General Control Principles]

Cinematic realistic texture, pure ancient Chinese Xianxia aesthetics, restrained deadpan comedy performance, observational cinematography, realistic micro-expressions, body weight, silk material, delicate film grain, volumetric air depth, and realistic 3D camera displacement.

The entire world lives continuously from the first frame to the last, but must strictly execute three-track authority:

Protagonist Plot Track = 100% screenwriting authority.
Environmental Life Track = Continuous movement authority, 0% screenwriting authority.
Background Character Track = Independent life authority, 0% protagonist interaction authority.
The environment must not create, trigger, explain, interrupt, solve, change, emphasize, or sync with any character plot. Wind, clouds, mist, light, reflections, buildings, distant characters, vegetation, and water bodies must not produce special reactions due to dialogue, eye contact, comedic punchlines, or protagonist actions. Camera movement can only be driven by protagonist plot and character blocking.
However, all non-protagonist areas must never be frozen.

Before formal generation, interpret all current reference images as the world's DNA, rather than frozen pixels or static background plates. Comprehensively understand the landscape logic, architectural vocabulary, scale relationships, materials, weather, cloud systems, vegetation, reflective surfaces, traffic flow lines, primary light direction, foreground-midground-background relationships, and off-screen space extension, then reconstruct it as a truly connected 3D location. Retain the identity and logic of the reference world, but allow for the replanning of spatial arrangements and camera entry directions, without mechanically replicating the original 2D composition of any single reference image.

[Characters]

Character A | Senior Sword Immortal Sister
East Asian female, 25–30 years old, oval face, fair natural skin tone, dark almond eyes, long black hair partially tied up and secured with a white jade hairpin, tall and slender, wearing white embroidered silk Hanfu, semi-transparent layered wide sleeves, silver waist seal, jade pendant, white cloth boots.

Character B | Junior Sister
East Asian female, 20–25 years old, rounded and lively face shape, black hair braided, petite stature, wearing green linen Hanfu, dark belt, wooden hairpin, black cloth shoes.

[Living World Continuous Operation Rules]
Throughout the 10 seconds, within every approximately 2-second time window, multiple non-protagonist motion sources from different spatial layers must be visible, but these movements cannot start simultaneously, nor move synchronously at the same speed.

Extreme Foreground/Background: A whole layer of massive clouds or air layers matching the current world, which has already begun migrating at a slow, steady speed before the opening.
Deep Mid-ground: Arrange 4–6 very small environmental characters living independently: someone walking continuously along a distant path, someone going up or down stairs, someone stopping to adjust sleeves or belongings before continuing, and two others naturally passing each other. All are unrelated to the two protagonists, do not look at them, do not stop for dialogue, do not stop because the protagonists stop, and do not synchronize actions for comedic effect. No visible background character can be frozen for the entire segment.

Mid-ground Air Layer: Thin mist, low clouds, or air volumes reasonably existing in the current environment continuously move around real buildings and terrain. Mist must be occluded by physical structures, becoming temporarily invisible after entering behind a building and reappearing from the other side consistent with spatial relationships, never penetrating physical buildings.

Foreground Layer: When the camera moves realistically, let a foreground element matching the current world—mist layers, plants, banners, building edges, or other reasonable objects—briefly pass near the lens, reinforcing that the camera is realistically located inside the space.

If water, wet stone, metal, jade, or other reflective surfaces exist in the scene, reflections must change continuously with the camera position and viewing angle, not remain fixed on the background.

All environmental movements share the same weather system and uniform wind direction.

The Senior Sister continues:

The Junior Sister immediately retracts all expressions.

The two face each other, about an arm-and-a-half apart.

No spells, no swords drawn.

Both strive to maintain complete lack of expression.

The Senior Sister almost reacts but forces herself to stay calm, only raising one eyebrow very slightly.

The corner of the Junior Sister's mouth almost twitches upward, but she immediately suppresses it.

A nearly imperceptible tremor then appears on the Senior Sister's lips.

Neither can actually laugh out loud.

The camera performs a slow, realistic small arc movement of about 15–20 degrees around the two. The camera must actually change physical position; digital zoom simulation of orbiting is forbidden. The background's near, middle, and far layers thus produce realistic parallax at different speeds.

Comedy must only come from the two's micro-expressions and restraint.

Meanwhile, the world behind them continues to live: a distant character continues walking and is naturally obscured by a real building, another background character naturally appears from behind another spatial obstruction and continues their route; air volumes continue moving between buildings; as the camera moves in an arc, the mid-ground structures and distant space maintain different parallax speeds. All background movements are out of sync with the protagonists' rhythm.

[Segment 1 End Continuation State | 9.5–10.0s]

The two protagonists' bodies gradually stabilize to facilitate the next segment's connection, but only stabilize the characters, not freeze the world.

The Senior Sister and Junior Sister still face each other, both clearly in a state of nearly being unable to hold back laughter but still forcing a serious face. Character centers of gravity, eye lines, and expressions are clear; the camera gradually stabilizes.

At this time:
Extreme distant clouds are still migrating.
At least one distant character is still in transit.
Mid-ground air volumes are still in motion.
At least one reflection or lighting state is still evolving.

This "characters stable, world still moving" state serves as the anchor point for the Segment 2 time connection.

[Segment 1 Specs]

16:9 widescreen, native synchronized Mandarin dialogue, restrained music, realistic footsteps, fabric sounds, distant footsteps, wind, and spatial environmental sounds. Background characters walking at the end of Segment 1 continue from their actual position and direction at that time, not returning to the start.
Clouds maintain the previous direction and speed.
Mist continues flowing from the actual spatial state at the end of the previous segment.
Reflections continue evolving.
The entire environment must never reset to the Segment 1 opening state.
Three-track authority continues:

Protagonist Plot Track = 100% screenwriting authority.
Environmental Life Track = Continuous physical movement authority, 0% screenwriting authority.
Background Character Track = Independent life authority, 0% protagonist interaction authority.

The background cannot cause the two to laugh, the environment cannot determine the winner, and distant characters cannot help complete the punchline.

[10–15s | Duo Close-up / Restrained Arc Movement]

Start directly from the accurate expressions of the two holding back laughter at the end of Segment 1.
Both continue trying not to laugh.
The Junior Sister changes strategy. She suddenly adjusts her posture to be extremely dignified, then very seriously mimics the Senior Sister's usual cold, calm, and solemn expression.

The Senior Sister immediately sees she is being mimicked.

A very slight change occurs in her nostrils.
She holds it in.
After seeing this tiny reaction, the Junior Sister's own lips begin to tremble more noticeably.

The Senior Sister then sees the Junior Sister is desperately holding back laughter, so the two begin to generate new feedback to "the way the other looks while trying not to laugh."

Escalate only through tiny micro-movements:
A slight eyebrow raise
A suppressed breath
A lower lip quiver
A nearly invisible shoulder vibration

Exaggerated funny faces or large comedic movements are forbidden.

At approximately 14.5 seconds, the two finally break at the exact same moment, simultaneously letting out a short, real laugh.

This laugh must come 100% from the mutual feedback of their expressions.

Meanwhile, the Segment 1 world continues running at its original pace: background characters continue their routes and are occluded by buildings; another person passes through a different route in deeper space; a third background character completes a tiny life action unrelated to the protagonists and continues forward. Distant clouds continue migrating, mist continues flowing, and reflections continue changing with the slight camera angle shift.

The moment they laugh, sudden wind, sudden light, background characters turning heads, cloud acceleration, or any synchronized environmental reaction is forbidden.

[15–20s | Mid-Long Shot Conclusion]

After laughing briefly, the two immediately regain their seriousness.
The Junior Sister asks:
"A draw?"
The Senior Sister thinks for a beat:
"Again."
The Junior Sister nods seriously.

The two solemnly return their faces to an extremely formal state, then simultaneously turn back forward and continue walking forward side-by-side normally.

After taking two steps, the Junior Sister casually glances sideways at the Senior Sister.

Unexpectedly, the same Senior Sister is already looking at her sideways.

Their eyes happen to meet.

The corners of both their mouths show the slightest tendency to laugh again, but neither speaks.

Do not add a third punchline.

Maintain an observational aftertaste at the end.

Because the two start walking again, the camera transitions to a gentle three-quarter side tracking shot. The reason for camera movement can only come from character walking, but physical spatial displacement must actually occur.

A foreground element matching the reference world naturally sweeps past one side of the frame; the two protagonists are in the mid-ground; at least two autonomous background characters remain active in deeper space. One passes through a misty area, partially obscured by the air layer before continuing; another moves at a distinctly different screen speed at a different depth.

The relative displacement of massive distant landmarks is very slow. Clouds and mist completely inherit the motion direction from Segment 1 and do not restart. If reflective surfaces exist, highlights slide continuously with the lateral camera position change.

After the protagonists' final eye-contact laugh ends, the background continues to move.

[Final 0.5 Seconds]

The two protagonists continue walking forward.

The audience can still clearly see multiple independent non-protagonist motion sources.

The joke has ended, but the world has not.

16:9 widescreen, native synchronized Mandarin dialogue and real short laughter, precise lip-sync, seamlessly continuous with the Segment 1 temporal state. Realistic camera parallax, autonomously moving distant background characters, continuous air movement, physically plausible dynamic reflections, and environmental spatial sound. The screen mainly features the two female characters, while allowing for very small distant environmental characters. No subtitles, no modern elements.

[10–15s | Duo Close-up / Restrained Arc Movement]

Start directly from the accurate expressions of the two holding back laughter at the end of Segment 1.
Both continue trying not to laugh.
The Junior Sister changes strategy. She suddenly adjusts her posture to be extremely dignified, then very seriously mimics the Senior Sister's usual cold, calm, and solemn expression.

The Senior Sister immediately sees she is being mimicked.

A very slight change occurs in her nostrils.
She holds it in.
After seeing this tiny reaction, the Junior Sister's own lips begin to tremble more noticeably.

The Senior Sister then sees the Junior Sister is desperately holding back laughter, so the two begin to generate new feedback to "the way the other looks while trying not to laugh."

Escalate only through tiny micro-movements:
A slight eyebrow raise
A suppressed breath
A lower lip quiver
A nearly invisible shoulder vibration

Exaggerated funny faces or large comedic movements are forbidden.

At approximately 14.5 seconds, the two finally break at the exact same moment, simultaneously letting out a short, real laugh.

This laugh must come 100% from the mutual feedback of their expressions.

Meanwhile, the Segment 1 world continues running at its original pace: background characters continue their routes and are occluded by buildings; another person passes through a different route in deeper space; a third background character completes a tiny life action unrelated to the protagonists and continues forward. Distant clouds continue migrating, mist continues flowing, and reflections continue changing with the slight camera angle shift.

The moment they laugh, sudden wind, sudden light, background characters turning heads, cloud acceleration, or any synchronized environmental reaction is forbidden.

[15–20s | Mid-Long Shot Conclusion]

After laughing briefly, the two immediately regain their seriousness.
The Junior Sister asks:
"A draw?"
The Senior Sister thinks for a beat:
"Again."
The Junior Sister nods seriously.

The two solemnly return their faces to an extremely formal state, then simultaneously turn back forward and continue walking forward side-by-side normally.

After taking two steps, the Junior Sister casually glances sideways at the Senior Sister.

Unexpectedly, the same Senior Sister is already looking at her sideways.

Their eyes happen to meet.

The corners of both their mouths show the slightest tendency to laugh again, but neither speaks.

Do not add a third punchline.

Maintain an observational aftertaste at the end.

Because the two start walking again, the camera transitions to a gentle three-quarter side tracking shot. The reason for camera movement can only come from character walking, but physical spatial displacement must actually occur.

A foreground element matching the reference world naturally sweeps past one side of the frame; the two protagonists are in the mid-ground; at least two autonomous background characters remain active in deeper space. One passes through a misty area, partially obscured by the air layer before continuing; another moves at a distinctly different screen speed at a different depth.

The relative displacement of massive distant landmarks is very slow. Clouds and mist completely inherit the motion direction from Segment 1 and do not restart. If reflective surfaces exist, highlights slide continuously with the lateral camera position change.

After the protagonists' final eye-contact laugh ends, the background continues to move.

[Final 0.5 Seconds]

The two protagonists continue walking forward.

The audience can still clearly see multiple independent non-protagonist motion sources.

The joke has ended, but the world has not.

[Segment 2 Specs]

16:9 widescreen, native synchronized Mandarin dialogue and real short laughter, precise lip-sync, seamlessly continuous with the Segment 1 temporal state. Realistic camera parallax, autonomously moving distant background characters, continuous air movement, physically plausible dynamic reflections, and environmental spatial sound. The screen mainly features the two female characters, while allowing for very small distant environmental characters. No subtitles, no modern elements.

Japanese full-color anime style. Japanese TV anime style. Cel-shaded anime. Anime-style screen capture focused on flat coloring.

Background is inside a mansion.

0-3 seconds: Front view of the black-haired maid character from Image 1. She has her eyes closed and is bowing her head.
'Lord Reis'

3-8 seconds: Close-up on the table. Several match-making photos are spread across the table. Comical impact line effect.
The voice of the black-haired maid from Image 1: 'Today as well, a large number of match-making applications have arrived.' The maid is not shown on screen. Dialogue only.

8-17 seconds: Cut 3: View of the upper body of the blonde nobleman from Image 2 from a diagonal side perspective. An elegant thinking gesture: 'Hmm, I'm in trouble.'
-> Background changes to a moe imagery scene. Dialogue of the blonde nobleman from Image 2: 'This is also because I am too beautiful!' Eyes closed, chin up, hand on forehead. Sparkling effects.
Only the voice of the black-haired maid from Image 1: 'What kind of stupid thing are you saying?'

17-21 seconds: The blonde nobleman from Image 2, sitting in a chair in front of the table, is looking at the match-making photos. Dialogue of the blonde nobleman from Image 2: 'I have to write another rejection letter.'

21-25 seconds: 'Is rejection the premise?' Upper body of the black-haired maid from Image 1, tilting her head curiously.

25-30 seconds: Blonde nobleman from Image 2 with eyes closed and arms crossed in a thinking gesture: 'I just can't help but compare them to you.' The black-haired maid from Image 1 standing nearby: '?'

prompt: Landscape iPhone video, one unbroken 30-second take, no cuts. LOCATION / TIME Hongdae, Seoul, blue hour. The pavement is still wet from rain. Neon signage is just starting to come on. Use a long, straight stretch of shopfront-lined sidewalk with enough clear depth for the performer and camera to travel roughly 40 meters continuously. SOUNDTRACK This is a music video. The track is the entire audio. The music is NOT playing inside the scene. It is a finished studio recording laid directly over the footage in the edit, exactly like a professional music-video soundtrack. The music must be: - Clean - Loud - Full-range - Mastered - Immediate and front-of-mix - Filling the entire frequency spectrum, including deep sub frequencies Music style: K-pop dance-break instrumental at around 104 BPM. Musical elements: - Hard 808 sub - Tight, snappy claps - Sparse minor-key synth stabs - Layered female vocal ad-libs - Stacked vocal hooks with no intelligible words Energy progression: The track begins sparse and restrained, then transitions into a full drop that carries the entire second half. IMPORTANT AUDIO RESTRICTIONS: NO street ambience. NO traffic noise. NO footsteps. NO crowd noise. NO voices. NO wind. NO environmental sound. NO room reverb. NO outdoor echo on the music. The soundtrack must NOT sound like: - A phone speaker - A car stereo - A busking speaker - Music playing from a nearby store - Music heard from across the street No muffling. No distance effect. No bandpass filtering. The music must remain studio-clean, full-frequency, loud, and immediate throughout. THE PERFORMER A Korean woman in her early twenties. Appearance: - High ponytail - Oversized varsity jacket - Cropped tee underneath - Wide black trousers - Chunky sneakers She is a professional working music-video dancer and immediately reads as one through her movement quality. She travels forward for the ENTIRE 30-second take. She dances for the ENTIRE 30-second take. The forward walk itself is choreography. Walking is never used as a break between dance phrases. Movement vocabulary: - Hip-hop bounce with strong, visible knee action - Chest isolations - Rib isolations - Shoulder pops - Waacking arm circles - Sharp wrist snaps - K-pop point-choreography accents - Quick heel-toe footwork incorporated into her traveling steps Movement density: Maintain roughly 4 to 6 clearly visible choreographic accents per second. The movement remains sustained throughout. She NEVER drops into ordinary walking. Every accent should feel rhythmically connected to the soundtrack. Her movement amplitude follows the music: - Smaller and more contained during the sparse opening - Increasingly confident as the track builds - Biggest and most explosive during the final drop Performance behavior: She occasionally half-sings along to the track without producing audible diegetic vocals. She catches the camera lens, grins, breaks eye contact naturally, then reconnects with the lens. She feels confident, playful, spontaneous, and extremely comfortable performing directly to camera. THE CAMERA Handheld iPhone footage. Landscape orientation. One continuous 30-second shot. NO cuts. The camera operator walks backward ahead of the performer for the entire take, matching her forward pace. Camera height: Approximately chest height. Framing: Keep her centered and framed from head to sneakers for most of the take. Use a wide iPhone lens perspective. She must remain large enough in the frame that: - Her face stays clearly resolved - Her eyes remain readable - Her hands remain clearly visible - Her dance details remain easy to understand Camera behavior should feel authentically handheld: - Mild natural hand movement - Slight rolling-shutter wobble - Small framing imperfections - Autofocus hunts once or twice - Exposure subtly adjusts as she passes bright storefronts Wet pavement and asphalt reflect the neon signage and surrounding lights. DO NOT use: - Gimbal smoothness - Orbiting camera movement - Zooms - Camera rotation - Slow motion - Drone shots - Stabilized cinematic tracking CROWD BUILD 0-4 SECONDS The performer dances forward alone. Ordinary pedestrians are already moving naturally through the background and around her. Nobody appears to know what is about to happen. 4-9 SECONDS One guy who is already visible behind her begins catching the groove. He starts copying her shoulder choreography approximately half a beat late. His participation should initially feel accidental rather than staged. 9-15 SECONDS Three or four additional people gradually join. Each dancer must peel naturally out of the existing pedestrian flow. Entrances can come from: - The left side of the sidewalk - A visible shopfront - Further behind the performer - Other positions already established within the shot Nobody should suddenly materialize or enter from an impossible location. Each person was already somewhere logically present within the continuous environment. 15-21 SECONDS The group grows to approximately 12 to 15 dancers behind her. They remain loosely packed rather than forming a perfect formation. They copy her accents with slight ripple delays. The timing differences should make the sequence feel spontaneous and contagious rather than perfectly rehearsed. 21-30 SECONDS The number of dancers now HOLDS. Do not keep adding more people. Instead, increase the energy. The group gradually tightens into a loose wedge formation behind the lead performer. Choreographic intensity reaches its peak. The lead performer remains the unmistakable visual focus. FINAL 2 SECONDS She throws her hardest, sharpest choreographic accent directly toward the camera lens. Everyone behind her lands the same beat with her. The movement hits hard and feels satisfying. The shot does NOT freeze. The dancers remain physically alive after the accent. Bodies continue breathing and settling naturally as the 30-second frame ends. BACKGROUND PEDESTRIANS Some pedestrians NEVER join the choreography. They continue walking normally around the dancers. Their reactions vary naturally: - Slightly annoyed - Curious - Amused - Indifferent Some carefully edge around the growing dance group while continuing toward their destination. This contrast between dancers and uninvolved pedestrians is essential for making the moment feel real. PHYSICAL REALISM Grounded human biomechanics throughout. Every movement must show: - Visible weight transfer - Proper foot planting - Real momentum - Believable balance - Natural joint articulation - Correct body mechanics No sliding feet. No floating. prompt:
Create a 30-second cinematic animated short featuring two original fantasy characters: a young female Taoist warrior and her gigantic reluctant giant partner.
Visual style: high-end Western animated feature film, stylized realism, expressive characters, cinematic lighting, detailed environments, polished 3D animation, natural physics, expressive facial animation, comedic timing, dynamic cinematic camera movement.
Keep the character designs completely consistent throughout the entire video.
Scene 1, 0-5s: The New Target
Begin with a quiet atmospheric mountain landscape.
A gentle mountain breeze passes through the frame. The camera slowly tilts downward, revealing the top of a large woven bamboo conical hat [from the reference image]
The girl's long dark hair moves naturally in the wind beneath the hat. The camera continues slowly downward until her face [from the reference image] is revealed.
She looks completely calm and slightly annoyed.
She picks up the phone and says in a casual, matter-of-fact voice:
"He's the new target? Got it."
She rolls her eyes.
Subtle wind, distant birds, soft mountain ambience, cinematic silence before the dialogue.
Scene 2, 5-11s: The Reluctant Partner
Cut to a dramatic wide shot.
The female Taoist stands on the edge of a huge mountain cliff [from the reference image]. Vast mountains, mist and clouds stretch into the distance.
Behind her, the gigantic blue-gray stone-skinned giant [from the reference image] is crouching on the ground, taking a rest. His enormous body towers over the landscape.
She casually turns toward him and says:
"Time to work."
The giant slowly raises his head with an exhausted expression.
He looks deeply annoyed.
"I haven't rested enough yet!"
His voice is deep and powerful, but his expression should feel more like an exhausted coworker complaining about overtime than an angry monster.
The Taoist remains completely unfazed.
Scene 3, 11-23s: The Car Argument
Cut to the Taoist walking confidently toward a rugged vintage open-top convertible [from the reference image] parked nearby.
She gets into the driver's seat, starts the engine and casually says:
"Come on, come on. Let's go."
The giant stands behind the vehicle, looking at the tiny car with disbelief.
He complains:
"Why do YOU get to drive while I have to run again?"
The Taoist looks back at him without sympathy.
"Then build a car big enough for you."
She immediately turns forward and drives away.
The giant stands frozen for a beat.
The vehicle disappears down the mountain road, leaving a small cloud of exhaust and dust drifting directly into his face.
He slowly wipes the dust from his face with an irritated expression.
Comedic timing, exaggerated facial animation, but grounded physical movement.

prompt:
CAMERA:
Realistic handheld DV camcorder aesthetic. A glamorous European brunette fitness influencer films herself in selfie and first-person style. Natural hand shake, slight framing imperfections, autofocus shifts, subtle zooms, occasional motion blur. Mix handheld selfie shots with a few fixed external angles using clean jump cuts. Never show the camera or her setting it up.

LOOK:
Soft vintage DV tape character, slight blur and tape noise, mild highlight bloom, subtle exposure flicker, muted contrast, realistic skin texture and natural indoor gym lighting.

STYLE:
Realistic late-night fitness vlog, playful, confident, slightly flirty and breathless. It should feel self-recorded and spontaneous rather than like a commercial. Fast clean cuts, natural body language and strong continuity.

CHARACTER:
Beautiful glamorous European brunette woman in her mid-20s, brown almond-shaped eyes, long lashes, glossy lips, sculpted features, lightly tanned glowing skin and thick dark-brown hair in a high ponytail. Slim, feminine athletic figure. Soft-glam makeup, fitted long-sleeve athletic crop top, high-waisted leggings, white sneakers and a towel around her neck or shoulder. No jewelry.

SETTING:
Quiet modern gym late at night with mirrors, dumbbell rack, bench, stretching mat and water bottle. Warm overhead lighting, mostly empty, calm atmosphere. No trainer or other people.

CONTINUITY:
Keep the exact same woman, face, hair, outfit, body and environment throughout. No extra people, duplicated limbs, broken hands, disappearing objects or impossible movements. No visible camera or camera setup.

STORYBOARD — 30 SECONDS / 10 CUTS:

1. (~3s) Arm’s-length selfie. She walks through the empty gym, slightly breathless but smiling. “Okay... late-night gym vlog.”

2. (~3s) Handheld pan across dumbbells, mirrors and empty floor, then back to her. “It’s basically empty in here.”

3. (~3s) Mirror selfie. She adjusts her ponytail, looks at herself and smirks. “I look tired, but we’re still doing this.”

4. (~3s) Fixed medium shot. Jump cut to her already beside the bench. She picks up dumbbells and gets ready. No dialogue.

5. (~3s) Same fixed shot. She performs controlled dumbbell presses, then lowers the weights and smiles. “That woke me up fast.”

6. (~3s) Walking selfie with towel over one shoulder, breathing harder. “Upper body done... and I’m already dying.”

7. (~3s) Tight handheld close-up. She drinks from the water bottle and exhales. “Best part of the workout.”

8. (~3s) Fixed wider shot facing the mirror. She stretches, briefly poses playfully and laughs. “A little stretch so I can pretend I’m disciplined.”

9. (~3s) Close selfie. Slightly flushed, she brushes back her hair and smiles tiredly. “I always say quick workout... and then stay forever.”

10. (~3s) Final arm’s-length selfie as she walks toward the exit, waves and smiles. “Okay, I’m done. Good night.”

FINAL:
Make it feel like an authentic self-recorded late-night gym vlog.

prompt:
Seedance Prompt | Dual-way Stubborn Apology Reversal

I. Project Positioning

Movie-level photorealistic quality, pure ancient Chinese Xianxia aesthetics, restrained relational comedy, elegant classical character blocking, Arri Alexa cinematic texture, clear and stable facial details, fine film grain, and natural volumetric lighting.

The core reversal of this segment is:
Two very proud people both actually want to apologize first, but neither is willing to admit they are apologizing.

The plot can only be driven by the characters' own intentions, dialogue, actions, and rhythm.
The environment is always an independently running, real-existing living world, but it must remain narratively neutral: does not actively trigger plot, solve problems, change character goals, create reversals, or express emotions for the characters.

II. Reference Controls
1. Character Reference
@Image 1: Used only as the identity anchor for Character ID A, the Sword Immortal Senior Sister.
@Image 2: Used only as the identity anchor for Character ID B, the Junior Sister.

2. Environmental Reference
All newly uploaded background and location reference images jointly determine the same environmental DNA. Before formal composition, silently deduce and integrate: actual terrain, architectural language, spatial scale, material age, vegetation ecology, water system flow, weather state, cloud and mist density, main light direction, reflection relationships, overall color system, atmospheric depth, and real walkable routes. Then recombine into a unique, complete, and unified new space that has never appeared before.

III. Character Settings
Character ID A | Sword Immortal Senior Sister
Same @Image 1 sister. 25–30 year old East Asian female, oval face, fair natural skin tone, dark almond eyes, black long hair half-tied with a white jade hairpin, tall and slender.
Always wears the same outfit: white embroidered silk Hanfu, semi-transparent layered wide sleeves, silver waistband, jade pendant, white cloth boots. Carries a unique silver longsword.

Character ID B | Junior Sister
Same @Image 2 sister. 20–25 year old East Asian female, rounded and lively face, black hair braided, petite stature.
Always wears the same outfit: bluish-green linen Hanfu, dark belt, wooden hairpin, black cloth shoes. Carries a unique dark steel sword.

IV. Core Props
The following props must be kept strictly consistent throughout:
One unique white jade sword tassel, one unique repaired white wrist guard, Character A's silver sword, Character B's dark steel sword.

V. Storyboard Script
0–5s | Wide or Long Shot
In the location replanned according to the reference images, the same two women walk from opposite directions and stop three steps apart. Clearly having just had a quarrel, both intentionally avoid direct eye contact. The same white-clothed sister silently places the jade sword tassel on the stone surface between them, saying in a deliberately cold tone: 'Your tassel was too old yesterday, it affects your swordplay.' Almost simultaneously, the same green-clothed junior sister also places the repaired white wrist guard next to it, answering stiffly: 'Your wrist guard was also torn, it affects your drawing of the sword.'
Requirements: Both visible from head to toe, spatial relationship clear, sense of awkwardness after a fight explicit.

5–10s | Medium or Cowboy Shot
Maintain same characters, outfits, items, and geography. Both glance at the item the other put down, then immediately look away as if nothing happened. The white-clothed woman pushes the tassel two inches closer, saying calmly: 'I just happened to change it.' The green-clothed woman also pushes the wrist guard back, answering: 'I also just happened to sew it.' Pause for a beat. The moment the white-clothed woman reaches for the wrist guard, the junior sister also reaches for the tassel; their hands almost touch, then both quickly withdraw and pretend to look at distant scenery.

10–15s | Close-up or Extreme Close-up
The junior sister finally picks up the tassel and ties it to her dark steel sword, whispering: 'So... about yesterday?' The senior sister lowers her head to tie the wrist guard, not looking up, answering calmly: 'What about it?' The junior sister pauses, finally understands, and answers: 'Nothing.' They look at each other briefly for the first time. Extreme close-up: The senior sister notices the junior sister tied the tassel backward; she silently reaches out to turn it the right way, then immediately pulls back. The junior sister tries to suppress a smile, whispering: 'You just never speak properly.' The sister answers almost inaudibly: 'As long as you understand.'

VI. Technical Specs
Total duration: 15 seconds. Aspect ratio: 16:9 landscape. Three continuous clear shots. Native synchronized Mandarin dialogue. Lip-sync precise with dialogue. No subtitles. Only two visible characters throughout. Consistency in face, clothing, props, and geography. Real movement in hands, silk, water, and air.

VII. Performance & Blocking
Characters: Both smart, restrained, dignified. Mature stubbornness rather than childish fighting. Intent to apologize is clear but language avoids 'sorry'. Comedy comes from misaligned expression and synchronized action.
Cinematography: Elegant and restrained. Captured moments: caring while not looking, hands touching/withdrawing, correcting the tassel.
Environment: Living but not scene-stealing.

Seedance Prompt | Turn an Intense Duel of Gazes into a High-Level Martial Arts Showdown

I. Project Positioning
Cinematic realistic texture, pure ancient Chinese xianxia aesthetics.
Overall style: Epic-level master duel camera grammar, restrained visual comedy, Arri Alexa cinematic quality, clear and stable facial micro-details, fine film grain, natural volumetric light, ample controlled quiet pauses, and precise rhythmic response.
Core Plot: Two true masters take a mundane act of 'staring at each other' and escalate it into a contest of martial dignity.
Hard Limits: No magic failures, no secret reveals, no environmental accidents, no clumsy character moments. All humor must stem from pride, competitive desire, micro-expressions, breathing, and rhythm.

II. Narrative Principles
Plot progression relies solely on: Intention, gaze, breathing, micro-expressions, pauses, rhythm, dialogue, and minimal physical reactions.
The environment must remain a vivid, active, and neutral world with continuous physical changes like flowing water, drifting mountain fog, swaying vegetation, shifting light, and natural parallax.

III. Reference Control
1. Character Anchors: @Image 1 for the Sword Immortal Senior Sister, @Image 2 for the Junior Sister.
2. Environment Reference: New uploaded backgrounds define the environment DNA, organized into a unified new space that respects identity and logic across three shots.

IV. Character Settings
- Character A: Sword Immortal Senior Sister (@Image 1). 25–30 year old East Asian female, oval face, white embroidered silk hanfu, silver belt, jade pendant, carrying a silver longsword (sheathed).
- Character B: Junior Sister (@Image 2). 20–25 year old East Asian female, round face, green linen hanfu, dark belt, carrying a dark steel sword (sheathed).

V. Core Performance Logic
The scene looks like a master duel but is a battle of composure and holding back basic human reactions. Humor comes from the contrast between the small event and the grand ritual.

VI. Storyboard
- 0–5s: Wide/Long shot. Two women stand 3 steps apart in a quiet space, sheathed swords in hand, staring seriously. Sister: "Today we compete in composure, not swords." Junior: "How?" Sister: "Whoever looks away first loses." Junior: "Bring it."
- 5–10s: Medium/Cowboy shot. Symmetrical composition, camera slowly pushes in. No head movement, locked gaze. Junior blinks slightly; Sister raises an eyebrow. Eyes become watery. Junior: "Sister, your eyes are red." Sister: "So are yours."
- 10–15s: Close-up/Extreme Close-up. Focus on eyelashes trembling and water in lower eyelids. They blink simultaneously. Quiet pause. Junior: "You blinked first." Sister: "You spoke first." Pause. Junior: "Draw?" Sister: "Again." Final shot: They lean forward slightly, locking gaze again. Cut to black.

VII. Performance & Movement
Characters remain intelligent and powerful. No exaggerated faces or slapstick. Precise micro-expressions: squinting, eyebrow raising, stable breathing, watery eyes. Minimal head movement.

VIII. Camera & Technical Requirements
16:9 landscape, 3 continuous shots, Arri Alexa look. Restrained camera movement from wide to close-up. Real volumetric depth and physical effects (hair, silk). Synchronized Mandarin dialogue. Seedance 2.0 Fast optimization for identity stability.

Duration: 15 seconds
Aspect Ratio: 16:9 landscape
Style: Cinematic Chase Oner, New York Manhattan street, cloudy diffused natural light, cold tone low-saturation documentary film quality.

Character: Protagonist

I. Narrative Goals
The entire video is a continuous horizontal side-tracking long shot. The camera remains parallel to the street, moving left in a shoulder-mounted stabilizer posture, without cutting or changing position.
1. Front: Tracking the running female lead to build speed and tension.
2. Middle: Briefly losing the subject due to foreground obstruction, with hesitant camera movement before locating pursuers.
3. Back: Focus shifts from pursuers to the distant female lead; camera recaptures and accelerates.

II. Spatial Layers
Foreground: Parked cars, passing yellow taxis, newsstands, construction scaffolding.
Subject Layer: Running female lead -> Pursuers -> Female lead.
Mid-ground: Outdoor restaurant seating, startled passersby, men in navy suits rushing out of revolving doors.
Background: Manhattan main street vanishing point, traffic lights, white steam from vents.

III. Executable Camera Timeline
- 00:00-00:01.8: Establish Stillness. Slow left pan focusing on an old man at an outdoor table.
- 00:01.8-00:02.3: Triggered. Female lead rushes past; camera snaps into a leftward acceleration with realistic shake.
- 00:02.3-00:06: Tracking Speed. Medium-close side shot of the lead at full sprint. Background is blurred. Focus on her tense expression and heavy travel bag.
- 00:06-00:07.2: Obstruction. A yellow taxi blocks the view; camera loses the subject.
- 00:07.2-00:08.3: Hesitation. Camera slows and drifts right to find the subject, eventually locking onto men in suits exiting a building.
- 00:08.3-00:11.5: Pursuers. Tracking three men in navy suits running through the crowd.
- 00:11.5-00:12.5: Focus Drift. Focus shifts from pursuers to the distant female lead; camera accelerates again.
- 00:12.5-00:15: Convergence. Camera tracks the lead entering a dense crowd. She is exhausted. Final shot holds as she disappears into the crowd.

The red line glows like banked fire beneath the frost, then becomes completely still. Reveal only: A SERIES BY MARA VANE The letters are carved into pale limestone, monumental serif typography, flat, centered, correctly spelled, and clearly readable. Hold the credit clearly. 3.0–6.0s: Small pieces of forged black iron slide across dark charcoal wool. A broken lance, a plain knight’s visor, a round shield fragment, and a small dragon-scale shard move separately, then lock into an original circular royal war seal. Two miniature armored riders cross paths once behind the seal, suggesting a medieval battle without becoming a full battle scene. The iron stops moving completely before the credit appears. No crest, no recognizable emblem, and no other text. 6.0–10.0s: An oval slab of black volcanic glass reflects the flicker of a brazier. Frost retreats from the surface and reveals the partial silhouette of an armored knight wearing a heavy wool cloak and a plain steel helm. The face remains hidden. Smoke gathers above the reflection. A huge original dragon wing shadow passes once across the smoke, followed by a brief reflection of orange fire and blue-white frost. Reveal only: CREATED BY ELIAS ROWE The text sits inside the clean dark reflection, perfectly readable and motionless.
